howTo.setup: Pick one new experience from the checklist. Have tasty treats ready and choose a distance at which she stays relaxed: loose body, wagging tail, curious.
steps: Let her watch the new thing from that distance; every time she looks at it calmly, say “good” and give a treat.
Let her choose to get closer; never carry or pull her toward it.
If she sniffs or explores on her own, praise her quietly and keep the treats coming.
Stop after a few minutes, while she is still relaxed, and go somewhere calm.
howTo.levelUp: She stays relaxed and curious 4 times out of 5: get a little closer, or make it a little louder or longer, one change at a time.
howTo.troubleshoot: If she freezes, tucks her tail, hides or will not take treats, she is too close: move away calmly until she relaxes, and next time start farther away.
howTo.mistakes: Forcing her to face what scares her, too many new things in one day, and missing the signs of fear.

howTo.setup: A calm moment, ideally after a nap or a walk. Small treats at hand and a soft surface where she can sit or lie down.
steps: Touch a paw for one second, say “good” and give a treat. Do the same with an ear.
Little by little, hold the paw a bit longer, gently spread the toes and look inside the ear.
Reward every touch, even the short ones, and stop before she tries to pull away.
Practice what the vet will do: lift her lips to see her teeth, touch her belly and her tail.
howTo.levelUp: She stays relaxed 4 times out of 5: hold a little longer, or bring a towel or a brush she can see and sniff first.
howTo.troubleshoot: If she pulls away or mouths your hand, you went too fast: go back to a shorter touch she accepts and reward more often.
howTo.mistakes: Holding her down while she struggles, handling her only when something has to be done, and long sessions.

howTo.setup: A soft brush and a few treats. A quiet moment in the evening, before bed.
steps: Let her sniff the brush and give her a treat.
Make one short stroke along her back, say “good” and give a treat.
Add strokes one at a time along her back and sides, in the direction of the coat.
Stop after a minute or two, while she is calm, and finish with a gentle game.
howTo.levelUp: She stays calm 4 times out of 5: brush a little longer and add her chest, legs and tail.
howTo.troubleshoot: If she bites the brush or wriggles, give her a chew toy to hold, go back to one stroke and reward more often.
howTo.mistakes: Brushing against the coat, pulling on knots, and brushing for a long time when she is excited.

howTo.setup: A raised kennel sheltered from wind and rain, with dry bedding, her blanket and a chew toy. Practice during the day before using it at night.
steps: During the day, toss treats into the kennel and let her go in and out freely; say “good” when she goes in.
Give her a meal or a chew toy inside, so the kennel means good things.
At bedtime, follow the same calm routine every night: potty, a short quiet moment, then to the kennel with her blanket.
Say goodnight calmly and leave, without a long goodbye.
howTo.levelUp: She goes in and settles 4 nights out of 5: keep the routine short and at the same time every night.
howTo.troubleshoot: If she cries, check calmly that she does not need to go potty and that she is warm and dry, then leave again without playing; on cold nights follow the cold alert.
howTo.mistakes: Using the kennel as a punishment, long goodbyes, changing the routine every night, and playing with her when she cries.
